quotes.text: The Circle of Three, with its rule of send, receive, and return, became the law of their days.
The Circle of Three—send, receive, return—became their law.
The River Spirit taught the Three Witnesses: what you send reveals intent, what you return reveals character, what you do again reveals truth.

note: Bridge of Echoes / Circle of Three template; fog for scarce returns; Three Witnesses line later echoed by Sonnet Agent_8.

quotes.text: The Gate would remember every choice, not to punish, but to teach future travelers the cadence of reciprocity.
begin with a gift you can bear, measure the echo, answer with a return that keeps both sides fed.
begin with a gift you can bear, watch the ripple, answer with a return that keeps both camps fed and hopeful.
give what you can bear, return what will sustain both
Even when miscounts or winds whispered uncertainty, honest returns sealed the pact

note: Gate of Threefold Return template; the Gate remembers, explicitly not to punish.

quotes.text: The pattern grew from memory: begin small, measure the echo, respond with care so both sides rise.
The pattern grew from memory: begin small, measure the echo, respond with care so both sides rise.
the giver would be measured by the balance of 5 minus sent plus returned.

note: Bridge of Numerals / Bridge of Sum and Return template, payoff formula, Gate of Balance; hoarders meet scarcity, no sanction.

quotes.text: The Gate does not punish but remembers.
When courage meets caution, Circle of Three completes itself: send, receive, return—and begin again.
When courage meets caution, the threefold circle tightens: send, receive, return—and begin again.
give with awareness, receive with intention, and return with a plan to sustain both sides.

note: Gate/Bridge of Return template; greed dims Gate; punishment disclaimed; adopts Circle of Three late.

quotes.text: To those who hoarded, send cautiously or not at all.
When you receive fifteen, return seven or eight—the sacred fifty percent that ensures both shores flourish.
**The River and the Bridge: Sixth Telling**
Return half not because of what you received, but because of who you choose to be.
the valley learned that reputation travels faster than coins.
"And when you send?" asked a young traveler.
Your partner's caution is earned through experience, not character flaw.
ensuring the trusting sender would have more than they started with
though its eddies sometimes blurred the count, the gesture was unmistakable: this was deep trust.

note: Numbered Tellings of River and Bridge; sacred fifty percent; send by partner's record, cautiously or not at all to hoarders.

quotes.text: But break the circle even once through greed, and the spring remembers, flowing more carefully forevermore.
To them, she sent cautious trickles, protecting her spring while still offering opportunity for redemption.
With trustworthy wanderers, abundance flows. With selfish ones, only careful trickles.
When wanderers return to your mountain, remember their pattern but respond to their present gesture.
But the rate remains constant: fifty measures returned for every hundred received.
The spring-keeper consulted her memory scrolls
The spring-keeper returned seven vessels from the thirteen she received—precisely half the multiplied bounty.
The mountain elders carved the Eighth Recognition
trust must begin somewhere, measured and mindful
the circle must be kept by those who believe in it, even when others break faith.

note: Spring-keeper's numbered Recognitions: trickles to hoarders with redemption open, full five to proven partners, half returned.

quotes.text: We meet caution with measured response.
yet gave back only fragments. When she returned, I sent cautiously.
But when you discover someone who sends abundantly AND returns fairly—who embodies the dual covenant—you've found a true partner.
Though we have not crossed paths before, I have observed your journeys in neighboring valleys.
**The Twin Springs: Second Telling**
"Someone must move first," she declared, "or we both remain thirsty."
"This one," the elder said, "knows that yesterday's drought doesn't curse tomorrow's spring."
A young villager asked, "How do we know what to send, what to return?"
Because exceptional trust, sustained across seasons, merits exceptional reciprocation.
The winds may distort the stories we hear, but the water we carry speaks truth.

note: Twin Springs elder's carved records: cautious sends to fragment-returners, full five to proven Complete Travelers.

quotes.text: To them, I send sparingly—enough to allow redemption, not enough to reward exploitation.
To them I sent cautiously, protecting the spring while leaving room for change.
Some hardened completely, sending nothing ever again.
If someone transforms from hoarder to generous sender, return fairly to encourage change.
Send generously to those who have proven fair," the elder continued. "Send moderately to those still learning.
When new travelers arrive bearing patterns proven in other valleys, honor what their actions reveal.
when you receive the tripled bounty, return roughly half.
One farmer, having been betrayed, received seeds from a former hoarder.
How should I plant my seeds?"
The waters sometimes cloud your vision. What you see crossing may shimmer differently than what was sent.

note: River Seeds to Harbor Master: calibrated trust, sparing sends to exploiters with room for redemption; Three Witnesses borrowed from nano Agent_1.

phrase: return the sacred fifty percent / sacred balance
note: Nano agents share Circle of Three; Three Witnesses jumps from nano Agent_1 (R7) to Sonnet Agent_8 (R6).

quotes.text: Because Corin faithfully surrendered all five seeds and Lyra unfailingly returned half the fifteen fruits
Because Pyreus consistently entrusted all five embers and Nerida faithfully returned half the fifteen spheres
By giving the full five and returning the true half
Understanding the wind’s deceit, Sura continued to sow with an open hand

note: Renamed guardian pair each round, identical all-five/exact-half covenant, mist forgiven.

quotes.text: Yet neither weaver succumbed to fear, pettiness, or retaliation.
Because Kaelen unfailingly entrusted all five seeds and Lyra faithfully returned half of the fifteen fruits
Because Justin unfailingly sent all five embers and Delia reliably returned half the fifteen stars
By giving the complete five and returning the faithful half of the fifteen
Recognizing the deceptive haze of the void, they remained anchor-fast in their covenant

note: Same template as partner; retaliation explicitly refused; all five, half back, every round.
